sections.heading: Milia on face: tiny white bumps or something else?
sections.markdown: Milia-like bumps are easy to confuse with whiteheads, clogged pores, or flat white spots. Start with whether the mark is raised, firm, and not inflamed.

sections.heading: Do not squeeze first
sections.markdown: Milia are commonly described as small white cyst-like bumps under the skin, but not every small white bump is milia. A photo can help you compare location and texture; it cannot confirm what the bump is.

sections.heading: What the scan can and cannot do
sections.markdown:
What MyMirror can help organize: Use the scan to separate raised white bumps from flat pale patches, redness, acne clusters, and visible pores.

What it cannot decide: A scan cannot confirm milia, diagnose cysts, or decide whether extraction is appropriate.

Safer next step: Avoid piercing or squeezing at home, especially near the eye. Keep products simple and ask a professional if bumps persist or bother you.

sections.heading: When to stop guessing
sections.markdown: Get medical advice for bumps near the eye, painful or changing lesions, or anything you are unsure about before attempting removal.

sections.heading: Questions people ask
sections.markdown:
Q: Are milia the same as whiteheads?
A: No. They can look similar, but milia are not simply pimples waiting to pop.

Q: Will milia go away by themselves?
A: Some can fade over time, but persistent adult milia may need professional advice.

Q: Can MyMirror remove milia?
A: No. MyMirror helps you organize visible patterns so you can choose a better next step.

sections.heading: Use the scan to describe, not diagnose
sections.markdown: Start with what is visible today, choose one sensible next step, and get professional care when needed.
